claims.text: Machine-learning optimization can design an automotive exhaust catalyst with enhanced catalytic activity and durability while reducing platinum-group-metal consumption.
Current automotive exhaust catalysts are commonly synthesized using conventional trial-and-error approaches.
Machine learning can predict catalyst compositions and microstructures that minimize platinum loading while maintaining effective active-site dispersion.
Platinum-group-metal dispersion and particle-size distribution on an oxide support mediate catalyst performance.
The computational method can identify non-intuitive combinations of support characteristics and active-site distributions that maximize catalytic efficiency.
Improved platinum-group-metal dispersion produces higher turnover frequency.
Improved platinum-group-metal dispersion increases catalyst stability.
Higher catalytic efficiency resulting from microstructural optimization permits lower overall platinum-group-metal usage.
The computationally optimized catalyst will have higher exhaust-component conversion efficiency than a conventionally designed catalyst.
The computationally optimized catalyst will deactivate more slowly than a conventionally designed catalyst.
The computationally optimized catalyst will require less platinum-group metal than a conventionally designed catalyst.
The predicted benefits apply to platinum-group metals supported on oxide carriers under typical automotive exhaust and accelerated-aging conditions.
